This article examines the distribution of [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] scores among incident male patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) across [[danmark|Danmark]] and its five administrative regions. The CHA2DS2-VASc score is a critical clinical tool used to assess stroke risk, with a score of 2 or higher generally indicating a clear need for anticoagulation therapy. Because this comparison draws from a single dated section, no longitudinal trends can be established; instead, the analysis focuses on regional variations in patient volume and the proportion of men meeting the treatment threshold.

Nationally, there were 11,462 incident male patients recorded, of whom 6,283 (54.8%) scored ≥2, thereby meeting the threshold for anticoagulation treatment [^src1]. When examining the absolute volume of patients, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] leads the regions with 2,949 men, followed by [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] (2,722) and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] (2,624) [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] recorded the lowest absolute number of incident male patients at 1,337 [^src1]. 

Despite having the highest patient volume, Region Hovedstaden stands out as an outlier regarding treatment indication: it has the lowest proportion of men scoring ≥2, at just 50.2% (1,480 out of 2,949) [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] has the highest proportion of men meeting the anticoagulation threshold at 59.0% (1,079 out of 1,830), despite having the second-lowest total patient volume among the regions [^src1]. The remaining regions fall between these extremes, with Region Syddanmark at 57.5%, Nordjylland at 55.8%, and Midtjylland at 53.8% [^src1].
